facts.fact: According to the U.S. Travel Association (third-party source cited by the page), tourism supports over 15 million jobs in the United States.
facts.quote: According to the U.S. Travel Association, tourism is one of the largest employers in the country, supporting [over 15 million jobs]

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative example, a town of 10,000 people attracting 500 additional visitors who each spend $200 could generate $100,000 in direct economic impact (a hypothetical calculation, not measured data).
facts.quote: attracting an additional 500 visitors who each spend $200 can generate $100,000 in direct economic impact

facts.fact: The page states that competing major destinations often have professional marketing teams and eight-figure campaigns (a vague, unquantified competitor claim by the vendor).
facts.quote: You're competing against places with professional marketing teams and eight-figure campaigns.

facts.fact: The page states that traditional TV advertising required minimum buys of $10,000 or more, plus expensive production costs.
facts.quote: Traditional TV advertising required minimum buys of $10,000 or more, plus expensive production costs.

facts.fact: The page states that connected TV (CTV) advertising lets destinations reach viewers on streaming services with budgets starting at $30 a day (vendor-page claim, Adwave).
facts.quote: lets destinations reach potential visitors watching content on Hulu, Peacock, and other streaming services with budgets starting at just $30 a day.

facts.fact: The page states that Adwave can run destination TV commercials on more than 100 premium channels (vendor's own claim).
facts.quote: destinations can create professional TV commercials automatically and run them on [100+ premium channels]

facts.fact: The page recommends that destinations increase their interest-based reach through specific topic pages, such as a page about "fishing in [your region]" that can rank for anglers' searches.
facts.quote: A page about "fishing in [your region]" can rank for searches from anglers.

facts.fact: A common benchmark cited for tourism marketing budgets is 2-4% of total tourism economic impact.
facts.quote: a common benchmark is 2-4% of total tourism economic impact.

facts.fact: For many small destinations, a tourism marketing budget translates to $50,000-$200,000 annually, according to the page.
facts.quote: For many small destinations, this translates to $50,000-$200,000 annually.

facts.fact: The page recommends posting on social media at least 3-4 times per week during the implementation phase.
facts.quote: with at least 3-4 posts per week.

facts.fact: The page recommends developing two or three pieces of substantial content (blog posts, videos, or guides) targeting priority keywords during days 31-60.
facts.quote: Develop two or three pieces of substantial content (blog posts, videos, or guides) targeting your priority keywords.

facts.fact: The page advises starting awareness-building campaigns at least 90 days before peak season.
facts.quote: Start awareness-building campaigns at least 90 days before your peak season.

facts.fact: The page advises increasing conversion-focused messaging 30-60 days before peak season, when travelers are making final decisions.
facts.quote: Increase conversion-focused messaging 30-60 days out when travelers are making final decisions.

facts.fact: The page states that trip planning often begins 2-3 months before travel.
facts.quote: Trip planning often begins 2-3 months before travel, sometimes longer for major trips.

facts.fact: Adwave, as stated on its own page, offers creating a TV ad for tourism destinations starting at $30 a day.
facts.quote: [Create a TV ad](https://adwave.com/try-free/) that showcases what makes your community special, starting at just $30 a day.

facts.fact: The page's 90-day plan recommends launching paid advertising tests with modest budgets across multiple channels such as search, social, and TV during days 61-90.
facts.quote: Launch paid advertising tests with modest budgets. Try multiple channels (search, social, TV) with small spends to see what performs.
